transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because the doctor who did my insurance physical said my weight was too low. I don’t really see it that way—I mean, I’m on ladders all day and working long hours, so to me I just look lean from the job.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah… I guess I do get worried about it. Like if the scale is up even a little after a client dinner, or if I had bread or something, I get tense. Then the next day I’ll cut back so it doesn’t stay there.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?
Not really. I mean, I eat more at a dinner sometimes if I have to, but I wouldn’t say it’s a huge amount or like I’m out of control. Usually I’m pretty aware of what I’m eating.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I don’t make myself throw up after eating.
Do you ever exercise excessively to burn off calories?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I exercise like that. I’m pretty active with work, being on my feet and moving around, but I don’t usually go work out just to burn calories.
Have you had any big swings in your weight over the past few years?

Not big swings, no. I mean, my weight has been low enough that the doctor doing my insurance physical told me it was too low, and that’s kind of why I came in. But to me I’ve always just figured I look lean from being on ladders all day and working long hours.
Do you think your weight is actually too low, or do you see yourself as being at a normal weight?

I guess I see myself as pretty normal. I know my friends and the doctor are worried about it, but honestly it feels like they’re overreacting a bit. I’m still going to work, showing up to jobs, getting everything done, so it doesn’t really feel like it’s too low to me.
Do you think you would look good if you gained a little weight?

Honestly, I don’t think so. I know that probably sounds weird, but when I see myself in a mirror or in photos—like next to one of my murals—I kind of judge how I look by whether my stomach and face look sharp enough. If they don’t, it can bother me the rest of the day.
Do you think your friends and family see your body the same way you do?

No, I don’t think they do. They’ll say I look too thin or that I should put on some weight, but I don’t really see it that way. I mostly notice if my stomach or my face doesn’t look sharp enough, like in a mirror or a photo, and that can kind of set the tone for my whole day.
Do you restrict the amount of food you eat in order to avoid gaining weight?

Yeah, I do. Most days I’ll just have coffee, maybe a protein bar if I’m between paint jobs, and then a small dinner later. I guess part of it is not wanting to gain weight, and part of it is that a full meal feels like it would slow me down.
Does your worry about gaining weight affect your daily activities or relationships?

Yeah, it does some. I still get my painting jobs done and show up for work, so it’s not like I’m missing jobs over it. But I’ll avoid certain things, like if a client wants to do lunch or if friends are going out to eat. I just don’t want it turning into people watching what I eat or making comments about how I look.
Do you think you would still restrict your food intake even if you weren't worried about gaining weight?

Probably some, yeah. I mean, the weight thing is a big part of it, but even aside from that, I’m used to keeping it pretty light during the day. Coffee, maybe a protein bar between jobs, then a small dinner. A full meal just feels like it would slow me down.
Is your main reason for restricting your food intake to avoid gaining weight?
Yeah, mostly. If I go to a client dinner or eat something like bread and the scale goes up even a little, I get really tense. Then the next day I start cutting back so it doesn’t stick.
Is your goal in restricting your food intake more about avoiding weight gain or achieving a specific body shape?
It’s more about avoiding weight gain. Like, if I have a client dinner or eat bread and the scale bumps up even a little, I get really tense. Then the next day I’ll cut back so it doesn’t stick.
Is there a specific weight or body shape you are trying to maintain through your eating habits?

Not really a specific number or exact shape. It’s more like when I catch myself in a mirror, or see a photo of me next to one of my murals, I’ll judge the whole day by whether my stomach and face look sharp enough. If they don’t, it really bothers me.
Is your goal in restricting your food intake to feel thin or to prevent yourself from gaining weight?
It’s more to keep from gaining weight. Like if the scale goes up even a little after a client dinner or if I had bread, I get tense about it, and then I’ll cut back the next day so it doesn’t stay.
Is your restrictive eating more about feeling in control of your body shape or about not wanting to gain weight?

It’s more about not wanting to gain weight. I mean, if the scale is up even a little after a client dinner or if I ate bread, I get really tense, and then I start cutting back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
Do you think you would still be restricting your food intake if you weren't afraid of gaining weight?

Probably not, no. If I wasn’t worried about gaining weight, I don’t think I’d be cutting back like that. It’s usually when the scale goes up even a little, like after a client dinner or if I had bread, I get tense and try to make up for it the next day.
Is your restrictive eating primarily driven by a fear of gaining weight or by a desire to achieve a certain body shape or appearance?

It’s mainly the fear of gaining weight. I’m not really chasing some exact look. If the scale is up even a little, like after a client dinner or if I had bread, I get tense and I start cutting back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
Do you think you would still see yourself as overweight even if other people told you that you are underweight?

Yeah… I think I probably would. Even if someone said I looked underweight, I’d still look at myself and focus on my stomach or my face. Like if I catch myself in a mirror, or see a photo of me next to one of my murals, it can kind of decide the whole day for me—whether I look sharp enough or not.
